function: system: over-the-air FL aggregation on single-antenna links, no RIS; p. 5: "channel coefficient between device k and the ES on width block j is denoted by h^t_{k,j} ∈ ℂ"
notes: PDF matches the DOI: p. 1 prints "DOI10.1109/jsac.2026.3726846" and the title "Optimizing Federated Learning Efficiency via Slimmable Neural Networks and AirComp for Resource-Heterogeneous Devices" (accepted manuscript, not fully edited). Excluded under code 6 (system), the first code that applies. Codes 1-5 pass: it is a research article that proposes and evaluates Air-FedSNN, federated learning aggregated over the air, p. 5: "AirComp is employed to efficiently aggregate the heterogeneous-width local models"; it designs that aggregation itself, p. 2: "A block-wise model sharing and width-aware AirComp aggregation mechanism is designed" (transmit coefficient eq. 10, reconstruction eqs. 13-15), so it would be area 7. Its Lyapunov and multi-armed-bandit width allocation (pp. 8-9) picks each device's sub-model width, a computation-load decision that the paper couples to AirComp, p. 8: "Width allocation affects AirComp aggregation quality via participation", so I did not apply above_phy; the reviewer may confirm. Code 6: every device and the ES have a single antenna and there is no RIS, p. 5: "The complex channel coefficient between device k and the ES on width block j is denoted by h^t_{k,j} ∈ ℂ", with scalar channel inversion by |h^t_{k,j}|^2 in eq. (10); the vectors of eq. (9) run over the symbols of a block, sent by TDM or FDM (p. 5), not over antennas. p. 10: "the wireless channel between device k and the ES is modeled as h^t_k = √(L(d_k)) H^t_k", where "H^t_k represents the small-scale Rician fading", for K = 20 devices within a 50 m radius of the ES. The words antenna, MIMO, beamforming and RIS never appear, and the terrestrial link is neither OTFS nor NTN, so the single-antenna exception does not apply. Code 7 would not apply (accuracy and energy results on MNIST, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet, pp. 11-15).
